text: The study projects that tropical cyclones could damage up to 182,000 residential houses by 2050 across the three focus countries, a 60% increase from the current 114,000 annually. Drought probability is projected to rise 60–80% among the three countries, with Cambodia facing a worst-case 46% increase in dry-season drought probability by 2080. The study also identifies transboundary drought spans from Cambodia to southern Viet Nam across the Mekong Delta.

metadata.solution_name: Transboundary Disaster Risk Assessment and Scenario Planning for Tropical Cyclone and Droughts in the ASEAN Region
